helix-date-picker.autocomplete: Renders a calendar of `<button>`s and no text entry, so there is nothing for a browser to fill. A property the platform cannot act on is worse than an absent one.

helix-dialog.cancel: Intercepted rather than relayed. `handleCancel` prevents the native one so Escape is a request the element can refuse, so it never completes: relaying it would announce a dismissal that was refused. `helix-close` carries the ask. See (296).

helix-drawer.cancel: Intercepted rather than relayed, as on `helix-dialog`.

helix-file-input.value: The native `value` is `C:\fakepath\name`, a lie the platform tells for privacy. `files` is the real surface.

helix-image.x: Where the `` sits relative to the root, which is the inner element's position inside this shadow root and answers a question nobody asked. A consumer measuring the picture on the page calls `getBoundingClientRect()` on the host, which is the box they wrote.
helix-image.y: The other half of `x`, and the same answer.

helix-list.reversed: The other half of `start`, and the same answer.
helix-list.start: This renders no `<ol>`: the rows are slotted and numbered by the CSS `list-item` counter, and that counter is not author-resettable. Measured in Chrome 148, `counter-reset: list-item 4` moves nothing on a `<div>`, on a `<ul>`, or even on a real `<ol>`, while `<ol start="5">` does and a named counter with explicit `::before` content does. Gaining a start means rebuilding the markers out of generated content, which is a different component. `type` is only `list-style-type` and is implemented.

helix-option.index: Derived from position among siblings, which the parent owns.

helix-pin-input.maxLength: A code is exactly `length` characters and the cells are what enforce it, so a maximum would be a second answer to a question `length` already settles, free to contradict it.
helix-pin-input.minLength: The other half of `maxLength`, and the same answer.
helix-pin-input.pattern: The filter is `type`, and it runs on arrival rather than on validation: a character the cells refuse never reaches the value, so there is nothing left for a pattern over the joined string to reject. One that disagreed with `type` would accept characters the boxes will not take.
helix-pin-input.selectionDirection: The other two, and the same answer.
helix-pin-input.selectionStart: The caret lives in one of `length` single-character boxes rather than in one text run, so there is no field for an offset to be an offset into. A consumer places the caret by focusing the component and the cells handle the rest, which is the whole reason this is not one `<input>`.

helix-progress.position: Derived from `value` and `max`, and readonly on the native element.

helix-radio.index: Derived from position among siblings, which the group owns.
helix-radio.label: The visible text is slotted, so the component renders whatever is given rather than a string it holds.

helix-select.autocomplete: Renders a `<button>` and a listbox rather than a `<select>`, so autofill has no control to write into. Real capability the platform has and this cannot offer. See (295).

helix-switch.indeterminate: A switch is binary by definition. A third state is a checkbox.

helix-time-picker.autocomplete: Renders no control of its own, composing `helix-time-input`, which carries the property. Setting it here would be a second place to say one thing.

helix-toggle.index: Derived from position among siblings, which the group owns.
helix-toggle.label: The visible text is slotted, as it is on `helix-radio`.

helix-video.onencrypted: Encrypted Media Extensions, which this component does not implement.
helix-video.onenterpictureinpicture: Picture in picture is not implemented. See `disablePictureInPicture`.
helix-video.onleavepictureinpicture: Picture in picture is not implemented.
helix-video.onwaitingforkey: Encrypted Media Extensions, which this component does not implement.

excusedEvents.helix-copy: A copy button announcing that it copied, which is not the clipboard `copy` event that fires when a selection is copied.
excusedEvents.helix-resize: A component reporting its own new size, which no native element event means: `resize` fires on the window and on an iframe, and `ResizeObserver` is not an event at all. `helix-before-resize` on Splitter is the request to move a divider and is a different fact again.
excusedEvents.helix-select: Native `select` is text selection inside an editable control, which is a different fact about a different thing. 294 measured the cost of taking it: `HTMLElementEventMap` is global, our classes extend `Event`, so an entry named `select` silently retypes every `textarea.addEventListener('select')` in a consumer's application as carrying our detail, which at runtime is undefined. Web Awesome keeps theirs prefixed for the same reason.
